Episode 245. Kinzelo's Cunning Plan (2)
That night, Lanke, Shagal, Bianca, Belact, and Badrei headed to the Mithra Desert.
The desert remained chaotic, still filled with lingering spirits left by the demise of Gliek, and the chaotic waste discarded by the forces during the old pagoda incident.
The region where Kinzelo's old headquarters was located, as well as the land of the corrupted water tribes, had been destroyed without a trace since the day Jin came out from Lafrarosa.

Mithra looked exactly like abandoned land. The remnants of spiritual energy obscured the sky, preventing the sun from shining even during the day, and something resembling chunks of flesh occasionally writhed on the darkened sand.
"Tsk, if my grand necromancy plan had succeeded, the legendary grand dukes of the demon world would be holding up fairly well by now," Lanke said.
"Lanke, you still believe that if it weren't for Jin Runcandel, that trivial plan would have succeeded?"
"Trivial? Watch your words, Shagal. Are you belittling it because you trust Lord Pirobs?"
"I only stated a fact, Lord Lanke. It's rather pitiful to see you clinging to a failed endeavor."
"Shagal... Lanke... Stop teasing. I... tried hard, really."
"What are you to defend me!"
"Ha ha, watching you guys makes me feel like the demon folk are just grown-up children mentally stuck in adolescence. Don't you think so, Belact? At least Bianca's naïveté is somewhat cute."
"I'm... not, naïve."
"Kahahaha!"
"Badrei, you too should recognize the gravity of our situation. We're here to gamble on Kinzelo's existence."

"I know, Belact. That's why I'm trying to lighten the mood. If we mess up here, and suddenly the enemy tribe brings an air fortress or the Vamel Alliance mobilizes to suppress us, we stand no chance with our current forces."
The five who had come to the desert were all vital forces of Kinzelo. If anything went awry and they were all buried in the desert, Kinzelo's future would vanish.
"That's why we all came here, to prevent such a situation. Once the lure is in place, Lord Zephyrin will also be on standby nearby, so we only need to keep a close eye on the enemy's movements."
Regular members, wearing protective clothing, began to take out various pieces of equipment from Grenil.

These were all tools that Lanke had used when attempting necromancy in the past. Added to these were inventions by Bubare, which did nothing more than emit flashy lights like signal flares (he named this 'party lantern').
Lanke skillfully set up each piece of equipment that the members had moved. The other executives were leaning back, simply watching.
So Shagal, intending to help Lanke who was complaining, reached for one piece of equipment, and at that moment, Lanke screamed out in alarm.
"Don't touch that carelessly! I'm telling you, all these devices are sensitive."
"...What are you talking about, Lord Ranke?"
"I mean, put down the device you picked up so roughly."
"Huh? We just agreed to pretend to do something grand, didn't we? Don't tell me, Lord Ranke, you are actually going to attempt necromancy again?"
"Of course!"
"Why would you do such a pointless thing?"

"We'll find out whether it's pointless or not once we see the results. Whether we're pretending to do something or actually doing something, as long as it doesn't interfere with the operation, what's the problem?"
Ranke was considering this operation as the last opportunity to attempt necromancy.
"Hey Ranke, you're really not one to give up, are you? Phew, this is getting more ridiculous! Isn't it, Berakt?"

"Hmph! We are in a situation where we must grasp at straws anyway. What if the necromancy succeeds? That would immediately add considerable strength to our Kinzelo. So, don't try to dissuade me by saying it's pointless."
"Ranke, dream... big. I'll support you..."

Ainas encouraged him, and Shagal looked at Ranke with sympathy, shrugging his shoulders. Berakt thought that Ranke's opinion wasn't entirely without merit. It was neither a waste nor a loss, and it wouldn't matter if it succeeded or failed.
"Do as you please. But if your obsession with necromancy causes even a slight hiccup in the operation, be prepared for the consequences."
And so, Ranke alone spent more than two hours installing dozens of devices. In between, 'wild lamps' were set up.

"Whew, it's all done. From now on, I'm going to focus on necromancy, so you guys turn on all of Bubare's inventions and dance or make a fuss, pretending to cast ancient cursed magic or something, do whatever you want."
Woo-woong-!
When Ranke activated the equipment, a heavy vibration began to spread in the middle of the desert. Ranke was chanting spells and drawing magical circles all around as if possessed by a demon.
The sight looked quite dangerous, and the party unconsciously nodded their heads.
"Wow, this would definitely give anyone the creeps. If I were the Vamel Alliance or the enemy race, I'd definitely want to find out what's going on."
"It certainly feels that way."
"Lord Ranke must have been deeply hurt in his childhood."
"Something, is exciting..."
The lamps were all lit, and it was truly like a wicked festival in the midst of chaos.

The lamps fired beams of light all around without rest. Though the desert seemed to be shrouded in mist due to the magical energy, this amount of light was enough to be observed from a very long distance.

"Great Lord of Flames, Karumashu! Oh, may your cruel flames burn the world once again! Masalrun, the long-time follower of the witch's sorrow! This Lanke calls you earnestly, appear before me and curse the enemies! Oh, oh, oh! Great demon of Tekan Mountain, Sriby..."
Lanke's eerie voice was making the desolate desert noisy.
Now, all Kinzelo had to do was wait for the enemies to take the bait. Praying fervently to the sun god.
The first to confirm Kinzelo's strange behavior were neither the Vamel Alliance nor the Jokmyeok, but Zipfel.
<1804, May 6th, 11:50 pm. Lanke Hallovich, Shagal Bahma, Bianca Caligo, Belact Sidlicker, Badrei Ramul. The five arrived in the central part of the Mitra Desert.>

<They plan to use the hidden Lafrarosa in the Mitra Desert to lure out the Vamel Alliance and the Jokmyeok. Currently, Kinzelo is purposely shining bright lights all around, attempting to summon ancient demons with necromancy...>
Tower of Story.
Elona was inside the transparent round device in the center of the tower, using the magic stone.
Fortunately, the tower gave her, or precisely, Kelliark, the 'record' she wanted. The record of Kinzelo's movements.
"Magic stone operation ended. Disconnecting."
Clunk! Whoosh, squeak...!
As Elona spoke, the thick tubes connected to her entire back and waist were disconnected. Her back looked almost melted due to the heat, and for a while, boiling blood flowed from the puncture holes.

But soon, Elona's body was wrapped in magic, and the wounds regenerated quickly. Dressing in the clothes handed over by the nearby waiting bio-golems, Elona's face looked more tired than ever. She staggered for a while, unable to walk properly.
"Hey, are you okay?"
It was Ragal. Seeing him, Elona felt a surge of anger, but she suppressed it and nodded.
"It's just a bit of overdoing it. To obtain a record of this purity at the current stage of the magic stone, it's inevitable."
Though she lightly described it as 'a bit of overdoing it,' in truth, Elona was in danger of receiving life-threatening damage at any moment.
She was indeed an immortal being when wearing the Holy Tube, but that didn't mean there were no limits.
"Phew, I'm relieved to see you say that you got the record. If there had been no harvest like last time, it would have been so frustrating."

The attempt without harvest was when she tried to find records about Shimat not long ago. At that time, Elona operated the Mashinseok (a magical device) to an even more dangerous level, but she couldn't obtain any information.
This was partly because the Mashinseok was incomplete, and partly because Shimat had not left any records in the human world.
‘Perhaps he may have a power of existence similar to the real Runcandel, although it would be on a smaller scale compared to Runcandel...’
The power of existence.

Elona thought for a moment about that strange power. Because of that power, the records of Jin and those around him were completely untouchable now. If she tried to pump energy to find Jin's records, the Mashinseok would refuse to operate to that extent.

‘...But it's strange. No matter how strong the power of existence is, the tower and Mashinseok's outright refusal to operate is absurd. Such an ability didn't even exist with Temar a thousand years ago. Really, could Jin Runcandel's power of existence be the only reason for Mashinseok's malfunction?’
It wasn't a problem that could be understood right away. Elona brushed off that thought and looked at Ragal.
“Is Kelliark on the top floor?”
“Yes. You look like you're having a hard time walking, why don't you rest for a while?”
“No, I'll go right away.”
“Stubborn as always, this one.”
“I'm not your friend.”
“Grouchy! Well, let me at least help you walk.”
“I refuse.”
Ragal shrugged and matched his pace with the limping Elona. As they reached the top floor, Kelliark turned to look at them.
“Elona, you're here. How did it go?”
“I've checked the records. Kinzelo is luring the Vamel Alliance and the Red Plutonian tribe into the Mitra Desert.”
Kelliark's eyes deepened. Elona conveyed the record she had just verified to him without missing a single letter.

“The people who would be most anxious right now, being marked as top-priority elimination targets by the Red Plutonian, I wondered why they didn't reach out to us... Kinzelo has played a pretty good hand.”
“Kelliark, my friend, a good hand? To me, it seems like a move that would ruin Kinzelo if either the Vamel Alliance or the Red Plutonian show interest in the Mitra Desert.”

“Ragal, I'm proud to see your intellect growing day by day. As you say, if one side doesn't take interest in the Mitra Desert, Kinzelo will be in grave danger. And that's likely to be the Red Plutonian. Jin Runcandel would be watching the Mitra Desert closely because of Lafrarosa.”
“Heh heh, it's all thanks to you, Kelliark, my friend.”
“What do you plan to do, Kelliark?”
At Elona's question, Kelliark smiled.
“It would be good for us, Zipfel, to lend some strength to Kinzelo's pathetic efforts. Both the Vamel Alliance and the Red Plutonian must search the Mitra Desert, so they cannot escape.”
